paragraphs.text: Be ye therefore imitators of God, as beloved children;
paragraphs.original: γίνεσθε οὖν μιμηταὶ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὡς τέκνα ἀγαπητά,
paragraphs.translit: ginesthe oun mimētai tou theou, hōs tekna agapēta,

paragraphs.text: and walk in love, even as Christ also loved you, and gave himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for an odor of a sweet smell.
paragraphs.original: καὶ περιπατεῖτε ἐν ἀγάπῃ, καθὼς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἠγάπησεν ἡμᾶς καὶ παρέδωκεν ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν προσφορὰν καὶ θυσίαν τῷ θεῷ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας.
paragraphs.translit: kai peripateite en agapē, kathōs kai ho Christos ēgapēsen hēmas kai paredōken heauton hyper hēmōn prosphoran kai thysian tō theō eis osmēn euōdias.

paragraphs.text: But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not even be named among you, as becometh saints;
paragraphs.original: Πορνεία δὲ καὶ ἀκαθαρσία πᾶσα ἢ πλεονεξία μηδὲ ὀνομαζέσθω ἐν ὑμῖν, καθὼς πρέπει ἁγίοις,
paragraphs.translit: Porneia de kai akatharsia pasa ē pleonexia mēde onomazesthō en hymin, kathōs prepei hagiois,

paragraphs.text: nor filthiness, nor foolish talking, or jesting, which are not befitting: but rather giving of thanks.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αἰσχρότης καὶ μωρολογία ἢ εὐτραπελία, ἃ οὐκ ἀνῆκεν, ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον εὐχαριστία.
paragraphs.translit: kai aischrotēs kai mōrologia ē eutrapelia, ha ouk anēken, alla mallon eucharistia.

paragraphs.text: For this ye know of a surety, that no fornicator, nor unclean person, nor covetous man, who is an idolater, hath any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο γὰρ ἴστε γινώσκοντες ὅτι πᾶς πόρνος ἢ ἀκάθαρτος ἢ πλεονέκτης, ὅ ἐστιν εἰδωλολάτρης, οὐκ ἔχει κληρονομίαν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: touto gar iste ginōskontes hoti pas pornos ē akathartos ē pleonektēs, ho estin eidōlolatrēs, ouk echei klēronomian en tē basileia tou Christou kai theou.

paragraphs.text: Let no man deceive you with empty words: for because of these things cometh the wrath of God upon the sons of disobedience.
paragraphs.original: Μηδεὶς ὑμᾶς ἀπατάτω κενοῖς λόγοις, διὰ ταῦτα γὰρ ἔρχεται ἡ ὀργὴ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῆς ἀπειθείας.
paragraphs.translit: Mēdeis hymas apatatō kenois logois, dia tauta gar erchetai hē orgē tou theou epi tous hyious tēs apeitheias.

paragraphs.text: Be not ye therefore partakers with them;
paragraphs.original: μὴ οὖν γίνεσθε συμμέτοχοι αὐτῶν·
paragraphs.translit: mē oun ginesthe symmetochoi autōn·

paragraphs.text: For ye were once darkness, but are now light in the Lord: walk as children of light
paragraphs.original: ἦτε γάρ ποτε σκότος, νῦν δὲ φῶς ἐν κυρίῳ· ὡς τέκνα φωτὸς περιπατεῖτε,
paragraphs.translit: ēte gar pote skotos, nyn de phōs en kyriō· hōs tekna phōtos peripateite,

paragraphs.text: (for the fruit of the light is in all goodness and righteousness and truth),
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ καρπὸς τοῦ φωτὸς ἐν πάσῃ ἀγαθωσύνῃ καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ,
paragraphs.translit: ho gar karpos tou phōtos en pasē agathōsynē kai dikaiosynē kai alētheia,

paragraphs.text: proving what is well-pleasing unto the Lord;
paragraphs.original: δοκιμάζοντες τί ἐστιν εὐάρεστον τῷ κυρίῳ·
paragraphs.translit: dokimazontes ti estin euareston tō kyriō·

paragraphs.text: and have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather even reprove them;
paragraphs.original: καὶ μὴ συγκοινωνεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τοῖς ἀκάρποις τοῦ σκότους, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ ἐλέγχετε,
paragraphs.translit: kai mē synkoinōneite tois ergois tois akarpois tou skotous, mallon de kai elenchete,

paragraphs.text: for the things which are done by them in secret it is a shame even to speak of.
paragraphs.original: τὰ γὰρ κρυφῇ γινόμενα ὑπʼ αὐτῶν αἰσχρόν ἐστιν καὶ λέγειν·
paragraphs.translit: ta gar kryphē ginomena hypʼ autōn aischron estin kai legein·

paragraphs.text: But all things when they are reproved are made manifest by the light: for everything that is made manifest is light.
paragraphs.original: τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐλεγχόμενα ὑπὸ τοῦ φωτὸς φανεροῦται,
paragraphs.translit: ta de panta elenchomena hypo tou phōtos phaneroutai,

paragraphs.text: Wherefore [he] saith, Awake, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall shine upon thee.
paragraphs.original: πᾶν γὰρ τὸ φανερούμενον φῶς ἐστιν. διὸ λέγει· Ἔγειρε, ὁ καθεύδων, καὶ ἀνάστα ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἐπιφαύσει σοι ὁ Χριστός.
paragraphs.translit: pan gar to phaneroumenon phōs estin. dio legei· Egeire, ho katheudōn, kai anasta ek tōn nekrōn, kai epiphausei soi ho Christos.

paragraphs.text: Look therefore carefully how ye walk, not as unwise, but as wise;
paragraphs.original: Βλέπετε οὖν ἀκριβῶς πῶς περιπατεῖτε, μὴ ὡς ἄσοφοι ἀλλʼ ὡς σοφοί,
paragraphs.translit: Blepete oun akribōs pōs peripateite, mē hōs asophoi allʼ hōs sophoi,

paragraphs.text: redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
paragraphs.original: ἐξαγοραζόμενοι τὸν καιρόν, ὅτι αἱ ἡμέραι πονηραί εἰσιν.
paragraphs.translit: exagorazomenoi ton kairon, hoti hai hēmerai ponērai eisin.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore be ye not foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο μὴ γίνεσθε ἄφρονες, ἀλλὰ συνίετε τί τὸ θέλημα τοῦ κυρίου·
paragraphs.translit: dia touto mē ginesthe aphrones, alla syniete ti to thelēma tou kyriou·

paragraphs.text: And be not drunken with wine, wherein is riot, but be filled with the Spirit;
paragraphs.original: καὶ μὴ μεθύσκεσθε οἴνῳ, ἐν ᾧ ἐστιν ἀσωτία, ἀλλὰ πληροῦσθε ἐν πνεύματι,
paragraphs.translit: kai mē methyskesthe oinō, en hō estin asōtia, alla plērousthe en pneumati,

paragraphs.text: speaking one to another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody with your heart to the Lord;
paragraphs.original: λαλοῦντες ἑαυτοῖς ψαλμοῖς καὶ ὕμνοις καὶ ᾠδαῖς πνευματικαῖς, ᾄδοντες καὶ ψάλλοντες τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν τῷ κυρίῳ,
paragraphs.translit: lalountes heautois psalmois kai hymnois kai ōdais pneumatikais, adontes kai psallontes tē kardia hymōn tō kyriō,

paragraphs.text: giving thanks always for all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to God, even the Father;
paragraphs.original: εὐχαριστοῦντες πάντοτε ὑπὲρ πάντων ἐν ὀνόματι τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρί,
paragraphs.translit: eucharistountes pantote hyper pantōn en onomati tou kyriou hēmōn Iēsou Christou tō theō kai patri,

paragraphs.text: subjecting yourselves one to another in the fear of Christ.
paragraphs.original: ὑποτασσόμενοι ἀλλήλοις ἐν φόβῳ Χριστοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hypotassomenoi allēlois en phobō Christou.

paragraphs.text: Wives, [be in subjection] unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.
paragraphs.original: Αἱ γυναῖκες τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν ὡς τῷ κυρίῳ,
paragraphs.translit: Hai gynaikes tois idiois andrasin hōs tō kyriō,

paragraphs.text: For the husband is the head of the wife, and Christ also is the head of the church, [being] himself the saviour of the body.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἀνήρ ἐστιν κεφαλὴ τῆς γυναικὸς ὡς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς κεφαλὴ τῆς ἐκκλησίας, αὐτὸς σωτὴρ τοῦ σώματος.
paragraphs.translit: hoti anēr estin kephalē tēs gynaikos hōs kai ho Christos kephalē tēs ekklēsias, autos sōtēr tou sōmatos.

paragraphs.text: But as the church is subject to Christ, so [let] the wives also [be] to their husbands in everything.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ ὡς ἡ ἐκκλησία ὑποτάσσεται τῷ Χριστῷ, οὕτως καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες τοῖς ἀνδράσιν ἐν παντί.
paragraphs.translit: alla hōs hē ekklēsia hypotassetai tō Christō, houtōs kai hai gynaikes tois andrasin en panti.

paragraphs.text: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself up for it;
paragraphs.original: Οἱ ἄνδρες, ἀγαπᾶτε τὰς γυναῖκας, καθὼς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἠγάπησεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν καὶ ἑαυτὸν παρέδωκεν ὑπὲρ αὐτῆς,
paragraphs.translit: Hoi andres, agapate tas gynaikas, kathōs kai ho Christos ēgapēsen tēn ekklēsian kai heauton paredōken hyper autēs,

paragraphs.text: that he might sanctify it, having cleansed it by the washing of water with the word,
paragraphs.original: ἵνα αὐτὴν ἁγιάσῃ καθαρίσας τῷ λουτρῷ τοῦ ὕδατος ἐν ῥήματι,
paragraphs.translit: hina autēn hagiasē katharisas tō loutrō tou hydatos en rhēmati,

paragraphs.text: that he might present the church to himself a glorious [church], not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.
paragraphs.original: ἵνα παραστήσῃ αὐτὸς ἑαυτῷ ἔνδοξον τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, μὴ ἔχουσαν σπίλον ἢ ῥυτίδα ἤ τι τῶν τοιούτων, ἀλλʼ ἵνα ᾖ ἁγία καὶ ἄμωμος.
paragraphs.translit: hina parastēsē autos heautō endoxon tēn ekklēsian, mē echousan spilon ē rhytida ē ti tōn toioutōn, allʼ hina ē hagia kai amōmos.

paragraphs.text: Even so ought husbands also to love their own wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his own wife loveth himself:
paragraphs.original: οὕτως ὀφείλουσιν καὶ οἱ ἄνδρες ἀγαπᾶν τὰς ἑαυτῶν γυναῖκας ὡς τὰ ἑαυτῶν σώματα· ὁ ἀγαπῶν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γυναῖκα ἑαυτὸν ἀγαπᾷ,
paragraphs.translit: houtōs opheilousin kai hoi andres agapan tas heautōn gynaikas hōs ta heautōn sōmata· ho agapōn tēn heautou gynaika heauton agapa,

paragraphs.text: for no man ever hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as Christ also the church;
paragraphs.original: οὐδεὶς γάρ ποτε τὴν ἑαυτοῦ σάρκα ἐμίσησεν, ἀλλὰ ἐκτρέφει καὶ θάλπει αὐτήν, καθὼς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν,
paragraphs.translit: oudeis gar pote tēn heautou sarka emisēsen, alla ektrephei kai thalpei autēn, kathōs kai ho Christos tēn ekklēsian,

paragraphs.text: because we are members of his body.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι μέλη ἐσμὲν τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hoti melē esmen tou sōmatos autou.

paragraphs.text: For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh.
paragraphs.original: ἀντὶ τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ προσκολληθήσεται τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν.
paragraphs.translit: anti toutou kataleipsei anthrōpos ton patera kai tēn mētera kai proskollēthēsetai tē gynaiki autou, kai esontai hoi dyo eis sarka mian.

paragraphs.text: This mystery is great: but I speak in regard of Christ and of the church.
paragraphs.original: τὸ μυστήριον τοῦτο μέγα ἐστίν, ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω εἰς Χριστὸν καὶ εἰς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν.
paragraphs.translit: to mystērion touto mega estin, egō de legō eis Christon kai eis tēn ekklēsian.

paragraphs.text: Nevertheless do ye also severally love each one his own wife even as himself; and [let] the wife [see] that she fear her husband.
paragraphs.original: πλὴν καὶ ὑμεῖς οἱ καθʼ ἕνα ἕκαστος τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γυναῖκα οὕτως ἀγαπάτω ὡς ἑαυτόν, ἡ δὲ γυνὴ ἵνα φοβῆται τὸν ἄνδρα.
paragraphs.translit: plēn kai hymeis hoi kathʼ hena hekastos tēn heautou gynaika houtōs agapatō hōs heauton, hē de gynē hina phobētai ton andra.
